categories.name: Arrays & Hashing
categories.whyItMatters: Hash maps and sets let you remember what you have seen so you do not check the same work twice. Google loves this pattern.

categories.name: Two Pointers
categories.whyItMatters: Two fingers walking on a list often beats nested loops. Interviewers watch for this instinct.

categories.name: Sliding Window
categories.whyItMatters: A moving window over a string or array finds best segments in linear time — classic Google warm-up.

categories.name: Stack
categories.whyItMatters: Last-in first-out thinking unlocks matching, next-greater, and undo problems.

categories.name: Binary Search
categories.whyItMatters: Halving the search space is how you go from slow to log-n. Google asks variants constantly.

categories.name: Linked List
categories.whyItMatters: Pointer juggling and cycles show you can reason about memory links, not just arrays.

categories.name: Trees
categories.whyItMatters: Recursion on trees is the backbone of hierarchical data thinking in interviews.

categories.name: Tries
categories.whyItMatters: Prefix trees shine for autocomplete and word search — a favorite systems-flavoured DSA topic.

categories.name: Heap / Priority Queue
categories.whyItMatters: Always grabbing the smallest or largest item fast is the heap superpower.

categories.name: Backtracking
categories.whyItMatters: Try, explore, undo. Interviewers want to see clean recursion and pruning.

categories.name: Graphs
categories.whyItMatters: BFS and DFS on grids and adjacency lists are Google staples for connectivity problems.

categories.name: Advanced Graphs
categories.whyItMatters: Dijkstra and topological sort show you can handle weighted and ordered graphs.

categories.name: 1-D Dynamic Programming
categories.whyItMatters: Remembering sub-answers so you never recompute — the core DP idea.

categories.name: 2-D Dynamic Programming
categories.whyItMatters: Tables of answers for two changing variables. Hard, but pattern-rich.

categories.name: Greedy
categories.whyItMatters: Pick the locally best choice carefully — prove why it works globally.

categories.name: Intervals
categories.whyItMatters: Sort then sweep. Interval problems appear in calendars, scheduling, and merges.

categories.name: Math & Geometry
categories.whyItMatters: Matrices, primes, and geometry tricks without heavy libraries.

categories.name: Bit Manipulation
categories.whyItMatters: Bits are tiny switches. Clever AND/OR/XOR solutions impress when used carefully.
